subject.title: Feature/Fix: Integrate lineage discovery and shadow accounting

question: Should CodexBar proceed with this four-PR lineage stack after its prerequisite, or first land the narrower proof-positive fork identity/cache fix and rebase or narrow the lineage work around it?
rationale: Both approaches target the same current overcount investigation and touch the same scanner identity/cache boundary, while this stack also adds measurable background work; repository intent is needed to choose the permanent architecture and landing order.

options.title: Prove and land the stack
options.body: Require exact-head cold, changed-input, and repeated warm-scan proof, merge https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/pull/2155 first, then review this PR against the latest main and the competing fix.

options.title: Land the narrow fix first
options.body: Prioritize https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/pull/2118, then rebase and reassess which lineage components remain necessary.

options.title: Pause the lineage stack
options.body: Keep legacy accounting plus the narrow fix and close the experimental stack if its additional accuracy does not justify runtime and maintenance cost.

recommendation.title: Prove and land the stack
recommendation.body: Require exact-head cold, changed-input, and repeated warm-scan proof, merge https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/pull/2155 first, then review this PR against the latest main and the competing fix.

likelyOwner.reason: The repository owner is the best available decision owner for selecting between overlapping scanner architectures and accepting the runtime tradeoff.
